Each returned EffectiveCapabilityGrantRow MUST atomically pair one active effective CapabilityGrant with the exact revision of that same capability_grant current result. That row revision is the only relinquish authoring basis; state_digest, evaluated_at, Event ids and locally folded history MUST NOT substitute. Unauthorized, missing and terminal grants remain non-enumerating. A query carrying at is evaluation-only and MUST be refreshed without at before authoring. After refresh or cas_conflict a client MUST obtain explicit user reconfirmation before signing against the newly read revision.

Optional query realm_id and cursor. Explicit subject and subject_station_id MUST be paired did_core_id values identifying an exact AccountId. Omitting both selects only the authenticated credential's exact AccountId. Handles, principal-only requests and inferred Station fallbacks are forbidden; self authorization compares the entire AccountId.

Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend kinds (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret_native); only backend_token shape is backend-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event carried in create_event through authority Event submission; the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service MUST NOT mint it, and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_id, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; the Circle scope stays plaintext until its own ak.mls.genesis is accepted.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through authority Event submission; payload.circle_id MUST equal the path circle_id and the complete target ActorId is payload.member_id. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event, nor add a capability verdict to the closed payload.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through authority Event submission. Path actor_id is one percent-encoded canonical JSON ActorId segment, not a bare principal DID; it is a route selector and does not rename the Event field. The Event membership MUST be leave and payload.expected_membership MUST carry the concrete current membership as its signed expected_revision guard; payload.circle_id MUST equal its path identifier and payload.member_id MUST equal the entire decoded path ActorId, including Station and branch. event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Event carried in grant_event through authority Event submission. payload.consent_id is the producer-allocated typed current result subject and the security-set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>', so the service chooses neither and MUST NOT synthesize the Event. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (the exact current authority-root controller; root_control_only forbids independent controller/Agent delegation).

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_principal_id defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent typed current result. On admission the recipient Station writes one holder-private ak.account.holder_quarantine entry with surface_kind consent_request, carrying no Event ref and none of the invite_delivery branch members; it shares the invite delivery quota, ledger and CAS chokepoint. Because this operation declares no idempotency key and carries no nonce, that branch deduplicates by live-entry uniqueness over (account_id, source_peer_principal_id, consent_scope). The written entry is holder-private service-local material, so durable_effect stays none.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Event carried in revoke_event through authority Event submission. The payload identifies exactly one stable consent_id and expected_revision; the governing Station performs an atomic current-row CAS and sets that Consent to revoked. No grant dots or revoked_event_refs exist. An any-scope Consent is independent: revoking it does not cascade to concrete-scope Consent rows; clients that intend to revoke multiple rows must sign one exact-revision Event per consent_id.
Lists holder-private consent typed results for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive typed current result state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent typed current result selected by the required peer query parameter. The authenticated actor determines the holder coordinate; peers never receive this DTO.

Holder-authorized deterministic compaction of the oldest contiguous terminal Contact prefix. The server computes the core from accepted history; callers cannot submit or choose it. Cross-service pairs use the continuity_checkpoint branch of ak.peer.contacts.command.submit.v1: the receiver recomputes, countersigns, durably commits and returns the complete checkpoint in one round trip, then the proposer commits the exact returned bytes. Exact replay returns the same checkpoint; same sequence with another digest is continuity_invalid and has no winner. Export reuses continuity_evidence on ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 and import reuses the Contact request continuity_evidence field.

Two-phase holder-local terminal reject. The service accepts only the holder-signed ak.contact.rejected Event bytes reserved for the exact current request slot, signs the matching rejection acceptance receipt, and provides durable exact replay/conflict semantics independently from normal accept responses.

Two-phase holder-local acceptance of one holder-signed ak.contact.requested fact. The accepted source receipt, peer closed XOR, full directional scope set and issuer-local slot lineage are durable replay inputs; no Private Consent Event is written or consulted. Recontact may import one generic mutually signed bilateral prefix checkpoint plus at most 64 uncompressed tail rounds. Missing material is continuity_evidence_unavailable; invalid, rollback or forked material is continuity_invalid. The same trust domain and exact ActorId pair cannot reset its lineage or founding slot. Missing continuity must be recovered or explicitly imported; a full tail without a bilateral checkpoint stays blocked. Only an explicitly initiated first contact for a legally different exact ActorId pair creates an independent root, without inherited checkpoint, history, audit identity, DM or MLS state.

Two-phase holder-local normal accept response. The service accepts only the holder-signed response Event bytes reserved for the current request slot, signs the matching normal-response acceptance receipt, and never writes Private Consent. Reject uses the separate ak.self.contact.command.reject.v1 operation. Glare is mechanically derived from two causally concurrent request receipts and forbids this operation.

Two-phase prepare/commit carrier for one holder-signed ak.contact.scope.update full-set directional replacement. Request/response establishes the issuer-local version 1 genesis; every scope replacement is version >= 2, exactly current+1, and references the exact issuer-local current head. Expansion and narrowing are both explicit signed replacements.
Holder-signed issuer-local lineage terminal. It consumes the Contact round and generation; it does not carry scope replacement and does not write or revoke Private Consent.

Authenticated holder projection from server-verified durable Contact evidence. pending_incoming includes request_event_ref and the exact optional request_message; respond/reject use peer and request_event_ref. Complete continuity_evidence is exported only for explicit boolean query include_continuity=true (default false); online recontact uses Station durable checkpoint and bounded tail. Private Consent and account-data notes are not Contact authority.

Authenticated exact AccountId selects its unique accepted PCR and current PrincipalResolutionProjection, independent of optional profile. Before the first accepted RealmCommit, only the exact atomically accepted genesis current is eligible while no accepted resolution successor exists; derived cache metadata is not authority. The own Station validates method history; no portable evidence or observation time is returned. Wrong or invisible account returns not_found; unresolved verified current state returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Authenticated non-enumerating read of exactly one closed Relation primary_conflict_domain or moderation_state target_ref selector from the current governing Station. The outcome binds realm_id, governance_generation, effective_stream_head and either one selector-identical present entry or an affirmative never_written selector from the same durable cut. never_written may supply expected_revision=null only for Relation create; moderation lift and Relation update/tombstone require present. Invisible, foreign, unknown and unauthorized selectors all return the same not_found and MUST NOT return never_written. Unavailable authority, incomplete coverage, timeout, stale generation, snapshot omission and holder-local history prove no absence. Consumers verify selector equality, Realm/stream binding, current governance generation and revision not ahead of the effective head before authoring; CAS conflict requires a new read, user confirmation and signature.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic recipient-delivery acknowledgement for one authenticated human-device or Agent-runtime endpoint (client-sync.md §10.1). The token covers one ordered queue containing both DeviceMessageEnvelope and MlsWelcomeDelivery branches; only this operation prunes it. Account stream and list cursors are read-only. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. The sender's exact durable device/generation state is checked in the queue transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and enqueues nothing. Each target carries a sender-assigned device_message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_account_id, sender_device_id, device_message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/device_message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1. Full endpoint capacity returns universal quota_exceeded before any batch queue or idempotency write; it never evicts an unacknowledged DeviceMessage or Welcome.

Reads the authenticated recipient endpoint's single ordered private queue. Each deliveries[] item is a closed device_message or mls_welcome branch; the same queue position, read-only cursor and cumulative ACK token span both. Human devices may also receive these items in account delta; Agent runtimes use their own current authorized endpoint and MUST NOT borrow a controller/device queue. See client-sync.md §10.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates. An encrypted DC has one immutable scope-derived MLS group and monotonic epoch lineage; the response carries exact current group_state_ref. Repair is an ordinary Commit in that group. If all private group state is lost, the old DC Realm is terminal and a new conversation requires a new Realm id. No second group, epoch reset or timeout takeover exists. Found MUST include coordinates.binding_event_ref naming an accepted endorsement for authoring. Clients trust their own Station current result and exact committed proposal decision; they do not replay a governance history closure.

Submit an exact producer-signed Event, MLS Commit, ordinary Realm bootstrap unit, Direct Conversation founding unit, or membership compensation unit to the current governance Station. Ordinary bootstrap uses the registered ordered slots in one Realm stream and one all-or-nothing storage transaction; success and exact replay return the same consecutive source RealmCommits without a batch-level receipt. Direct Conversation founding is its own ordered four-Event all-or-nothing unit with a separate founding-slot fence; success and exact replay return the same four consecutive source RealmCommits, whose fourth committed_at is the sole acceptance time. No founding receipt exists. Compensation carries closed transport-only evidence and a single-use CAS. canonical_hash/full_body remains the operation replay identity for every branch; no arbitrary atomic Event batch is admitted.

Return the complete durable frozen fanout target set for one caller-visible accepted Event. Unknown and invisible Events share not_found. Rows use stable opaque target_id and are sorted byte-wise; service_id is included only when the caller can currently read an exact contributing joined-member ActorId routing projection. The query has no retry, route-resolution or delivery state side effect.
Read one authorized Realm, Circle, or Sidecar stream by continuous stream_position.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Authorized account-internal resolution audit evidence: PCR realm id, genesis Event and receipt, current and bounded predecessor resolution Events, and an accepted RealmCommit covering the disclosed state. Authorization is only a current holder session bound to the exact account_id; recovery first completes the existing recovery transaction and becomes the current holder rather than introducing a second audit authorization path. Unknown account, wrong AccountId and unauthorized caller share one anti-enumeration outcome. history_depth is the closed range 0..256 with default 0 and MUST NOT be silently capped; after_resolution_event_ref stops the disclosed segment exclusively at a known ancestor in this account's lineage and requires history_depth >= 1. A truncated segment sets history_complete=false and returns next_audit_cursor; omitted history is unknown, never absent.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. account_id is server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone.v1(block_peer) denied_subjects writes.

Authenticated client dispatch of private invite evidence through the inviter Station. invite_event_id must resolve to an Event already accepted by this service and authored by the current session actor. The service reads its own stored canonical Event bytes; local delivery reuses the peer receive policy path and remote delivery builds the peer request from those bytes.

Issues the durable, single-use, short-TTL (<=300s) challenge that every high-risk backup delete proof must sign over. While a challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid the service returns the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new one. See key-management.md section 7.8.1.
Issue a durable current-device-only challenge with lifetime at most 300 seconds. Recovery unlock reuses its recovery session challenge.
Same still-authorized holder exact replay returns the durable unlock outcome without charging the one-use challenge again.

High-risk delete guarded by a server-issued single-use challenge and the shared high-risk authority proof family (key-management.md section 7.8/7.8.1). The challenge is consumed atomically with the first successful delete; a byte-identical retry returns the same empty success response, and the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

Session-authenticated entry to the canonical KeyPackage claim carrier. The participant supplies the same closed device|agent requester_authorization and stable service_binding with source/destination service DIDs used by peer claim; deployment trust domains are absent from participant-authored bytes and are bound only by the Station's verified resolution plus outer RFC 9421 headers. The local Station verifies the current durable requester authorization and exact current joined-member ActorId routing projection; local source=destination uses the same destination-authority CAS, while remote targets are durably relayed without rewriting the participant-signed body. Uncertain outcomes are queried by the original claim_request_id and request digest before any exact resend.

Authenticated cross-account device directory and published prekey-bundle read. Selectors are bounded at 1..16 accounts and 32 devices each with a 64 KiB canonical request; an over-limit request fails whole. Disclosure requires a current authorization relationship - a Realm the requester still joins, or a current Contact/call/session context, where the Contact case never requires a shared Realm. Targets hosted by another Station are resolved through ak.peer.keys.read.lookup.v1 and verified locally before the row is returned; the client never contacts a foreign Station and its session credential is never forwarded. failures[].reason_code is the closed pair device_result_unavailable and device_directory_unavailable, and an unavailable fetch is never rendered as an empty device set.

Own-Station verified route and signing keys for the media service anchored by one joined Realm current accepted realm_media_service typed current result. Membership visibility and the anchored typed current result are evaluated under one confirmed basis with exactly one head per Realm; the caller supplies no service id, DID, base URL or candidate origin. The result resolves service identity, purpose and route only: it releases no media key, no backend token and no plaintext-visibility authorization, and expires_at bounds route and key reuse to at most 300 seconds. Invisible Realm or absent anchor returns not_found; unresolved accepted state returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and complete response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Prepare one complete unsigned ak.message.create from a closed intent, after client encryption where required. Exact canonical request replay; expires at client created_at plus 300 seconds. No sequence reservation and no submit ticket.

durable_effect.rationale: Only a bounded expiring preparation cache; no accepted Event, sequence, membership or projection mutation.

operations.notes: Carries one caller-signed moderation report Event. The current governance Station revalidates the authenticated reporter, target visibility, effective scope and current authorization, then commits the exact Event on that scope's authority stream. The Event contains only its closed producer, scope, payload and signature fields.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Accepts exactly one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 cursor; envelope.actor_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated holder, payload.device_id MUST equal the authenticated session device, and envelope.realm_id MUST equal payload.realm_id. The service validates and forwards the exact Event bytes and MUST NOT rebuild the payload or co-sign. The cursor object carries neither an id nor an updated_at — a cursor is never updated in place, its identity is the (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) tuple and there is no read_cursor typed ID kind — so the update time of an advance is the Event envelope created_at, and the read_marker_outcome updated_at is that derived envelope time of the winning advance. Sibling devices observe the winner as the ak.read_cursor.update device message whose content is ak.schema.read_cursor_update.v1. Multi-device convergence is causal-first per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md section 6.5: a position that causally dominates the other wins regardless of HLC; HLC max applies only to causally concurrent positions, and device_id lexicographic order only breaks equal HLCs. The cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.

ACL-filtered paginated enumeration of the authority streams of one Realm that the caller is permitted to know exist and whose Commit chain is established. It is core, not an extension read: positional scan requires a stream_ref the caller already holds and the subscribe window is bounded to 64 streams, so without enumeration a stream outside the first screen would be undiscoverable and could starve. Pagination is one fixed server-side generation with a per-page permission recheck; a stream that appears later is discovered by a later enumeration or by the visible discovery delta, never inserted into an earlier page. Containers with no Commit yet are omitted rather than reported with an empty head.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Prepares one join, knock or invite acceptance against the Realm's current governance Station. The Station is discovered from the current authority bundle, not from the inviter or genesis Station. Preparation freezes the exact request and current policy revision; final admission is an authority commit and performs no actor-checkpoint, RealmCommit-basis or authority-commit calculation.

Own-Station validated progress of one join application authored by this account before membership exists. account_id MUST equal the complete account of the authenticated session and its Station MUST be the service handling the request. origin_state reports this Station's own durable forwarding fact and is never Realm acceptance; realm_state appears only after a bounded candidate answered, and accepted_commit_id appears only when this Station has itself verified and accepted the covering RealmCommit. The outcome carries no Ack, authority set, authority signature or RealmCommit bytes: after committed the account is a member and continues through the ordinary member federation and sync surfaces. Unknown Event, another account's application and a non-matching session share one non-enumerating not_found.

Own-Station validated pre-join Realm preview. account_id MUST equal the complete account of the authenticated session and its Station MUST be the service handling the request. The invite target is resolved only against inviter_account_id.station_id, taking the equivalent local path when that Station is this service; every other target is resolved through the Directory discovery input surface and independently validated before it becomes a result. The client never calls the source, never selects a forwarding candidate and never goes back to a truth source: join_candidates, source_refs, stale and divergent are omitted. request_digest binds the exact chosen target, and source names where the disclosure came from. An unreachable source is a retryable upstream failure and MUST NOT be replaced by another service identity or another Realm member Station.
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organization_ids hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hint_ids are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

Required query realm_id. Returns the exact previously issued closed signed snapshot identified by snapshot_id only to the same authenticated account while Realm and every disclosed row/head/floor remain authorized. A referenced non-preview window requires durable exact retrieval for its consumption lifetime; unavailable references require per-stream preview_only. Response IDs MUST exactly match request IDs; never regenerate, resign or substitute current head.

Continues only the canonical next transaction step. Recovery's terminal step carries the replacement-device-signed recovery receipt; the current governance Station atomically validates both prepared producer Events, issues their two consecutive PCR-stream RealmCommits, advances device generation, activates the device and consumes the session. The client never supplies or signs either RealmCommit.

Creates exactly one durable RecoveryTransaction or SecurityRotationTransaction. The coordinator MUST atomically persist canonical request bytes, request_digest, the closed typed prepared_plan and prepared_plan_digest, all reserved public ids, and the initial resource before the first irreversible side effect. Recovery create also CAS-binds one already verified recovery session to this transaction. SecurityRotation create requires fresh high-risk action authentication judged by the Account Authority and binds authorizing_device_id to the authenticated session; it issues no AuthorizationLease. Same transaction_id plus identical bytes returns the recorded resource; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Authoritative durable progress query by transaction_id. It MUST return the prepared plan, accepted step prefix and optional terminal result; callers derive the next action from kind plus prefix length. It MUST NOT synthesize progress from a short-lived HTTP idempotency cache.
Transient encrypted Signal rail. It creates no durable Event or RealmCommit, does not advance any authority stream, and grants no delivery or authorization proof.

Authenticated encrypted-only Signal Extension receive rail. Frames carry SignalEnvelope objects or bounded transport control frames; exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. No catch-up or durable delivery guarantee.

Own Station validates 1..64 exact account-device/Agent current or historical selectors. Current keys serve this validation invocation only. Each historical selector requires committed_event_ref copied from one verified account-subscribe or per-stream-scan stream_row; its stream Realm must equal request.realm_id. A bare EventId, current projection, cursor, timestamp, arrival order or cached sighting cannot supply the coordinate, and missing or redacted history remains unavailable without current-query fallback. Every resolved key independently carries its accepted authorization_ref as another committed_event_ref plus the verified current revision and governance generation of that authorization stream; the target and authorization refs may differ and must never be forced equal. Exactly one resolved/unavailable result maps by complete selector equality rather than array position; unavailable echoes that complete selector. Request <=64 KiB; each result <=16 KiB; complete response <=1 MiB. No third history carrier, portable closure, caller-selected receiver, or current-directory substitution for history.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Exact non-enumerating self watch current read from the governing Station's durable typed reducer under one confirmed governance generation and effective-scope authorization basis. Request watcher_actor_id MUST be the current authenticated effective ActorId; writing another actor under ak.strand.watch.set.others does not grant this read. Response discriminates never_written from current, including a written value:null with a real revision. Invisible/foreign/unknown selectors collapse to not_found; unresolved current authority returns revision_unavailable. The returned stream head and generation are observations, not future CAS authority. No snapshot omission, local raw Event order or default level proves absence.

Purpose-scoped acceptance attestation the authenticated inviter obtains from its own Station for one exact ak.invite.third_party it authored (third-party-invites.md section 7.4). The Station evaluates its current accepted basis, confirms the caller authored the invite, that the invite typed current result is pending, and that verification_id matches the typed current result and the current allowlist, then signs an attestation binding station_id, verification_id, audience, realm_id, invite_id, inviter_account_id, provisioning_id, the exact public material, invite_expires_at, invite_state, accepted_commit_id, observed_at and its own expires_at. The caller supplies no governance material and receives no governance closure, RealmCommit ancestry or membership listing; the attestation authorizes nothing except activation of the named provisioning record. Not visible, not authored by the caller and not pending all return the uniform section 6 not_found; a basis the Station cannot currently confirm returns revision_unavailable.
